record.provider: Lemmy + pict-rs — per-instance image store, no per-user quota

free_tier.stated: No per-user quota in Lemmy's own schema — the bound is pict-rs (the separate Rust image server) and the instance's disk. Upload is gated per-instance by the `image_upload` / `image_mode` local-site flag rather than by bytes.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap set by pict-rs (`max_file_size`, commonly 40 MB

record.tooling: Lemmy API v3: POST /api/v3/pictrs/image (multipart) or /api/v3/upload; needs a JWT from POST /api/v3/user/login. pict-rs itself exposes POST /image on its own port (often 8080). On instances that expose it, that is a cleaner upload path than the Lemmy API.
record.chaining: Lemmy is the weakest of the family: most large instances now REQUIRE an application (lemmy.world registration_mode = 'RequireApplication'), and `image_mode` is frequently set to block uploads entirely or to proxy-only. Multiplier depends entirely on finding a permissive instance.

record.limits_note: per-object-cap set by pict-rs (`max_file_size`, commonly 40 MB); no per-user byte quota; per-instance disk.
record.reliability_note: Registration gated on the big instances. Also note Lemmy stores federated/remote images too, so operator disk fills from other people's content, which is why uploads get turned off.

evidence.proved: probe: GET -> 200, local_site.registration_mode='RequireApplication', version 0.19.19-9-gc55dd1b1a; local_site carries NO image upload size field (only image_mode/enable_nsfw-style flags) — confirms the quota lives in pict-rs, not Lemmy
pict-rs is a separate service; 'Generate thumbnails for external post urls and store them persistently in pict-rs. This also increases storage usage.'
